system.description:
Apply only the Expertise benefit of this known stance.

You have learned how to fight with the precision and ferociousness of a serpent: You fight with your fingers held to a point as your stab into an opponent’s pressure points like needles during acupuncture.

Your [Unarmed Damage] die becomes a d6 and piercing.

Once per turn, when you hit a creature with an unarmed attack, they gain a -1 penalty to their next d20 roll before the end of their next turn.

Beginning at 5th level, Once per turn, in place of one of your attacks granted by the Attack action or when you make a melee Taijutsu attack, you can perform a Serpent Grasp.

Serpent Grasp. Make an unarmed attack against a creature within your reach. On a hit, deal your [Unarmed Damage] and attempt to Grapple them using only one hand. While you have a creature Grappled this way, you can use an attack granted by the Attack action to use the enemy you are grappling as a weapon, swinging them into others, with the Serpents Rattle attack.

Serpents Rattle. While you are grappling a creature as a result of Serpents Grasp, you can force them to make a Strength saving throw vs your Taijutsu save DC. On a failure, you swing them like the end of a snakes tail, making an unarmed attack targeting a different creature, striking them with the grappled creature, dealing your [Unarmed Damage] + 2d6 to both the grappled creature and the target of the attack.

Beginning at 10th level, while you have a creature grappled as a result of Serpents Grasp they always suffer a -2 penalty to their first d20 roll per turn. This does not stack with this stances -1 penalty.
